conventions.commits: Conventional commits with feat/fix/chore prefixes; signed commits (DCO); issue references in PR titles
conventions.testing: Integration tests in crates/aptu-coder-core/tests/integration_tests.rs; unit tests in language modules; test_* functions verify query compilation, element extraction, and inheritance extraction
conventions.linting: cargo clippy with -D warnings enforced; workspace lints: undocumented_unsafe_blocks, unwrap_used, expect_used (with test exemptions); cargo fmt --check; cargo deny check advisories licenses
conventions.error_handling: thiserror for error types; Result<T, E> returns; no panics in production code; test code has exemptions for unwrap/expect via cfg_attr

patterns: Each language has a module in crates/aptu-coder-core/src/languages/<lang>.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, and optional REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY constants
ELEMENT_QUERY captures @function and @class nodes with name fields; @class includes interfaces, traits, enums
DEFUSE_QUERY captures write sites (assignments, declarations) and read sites (identifier usage) for def-use analysis
extract_inheritance() handler walks parent class/interface fields and returns Vec<String> with 'extends'/'implements' prefixes
Language is registered in get_language_info() match statement in mod.rs with LanguageInfo struct containing all handlers and queries
Language is registered in get_ts_language() match statement in mod.rs returning tree-sitter Language object
File extension mapped in lang.rs EXTENSION_MAP constant as (&str, &str) tuples
tree-sitter-<lang> crate added to workspace dependencies in Cargo.toml and crates/aptu-coder-core/Cargo.toml
Language module imported via pub mod <lang> in mod.rs
Integration tests added to crates/aptu-coder-core/tests/integration_tests.rs verifying element extraction and inheritance
constraints: All languages are unconditionally compiled in; no feature gates
DEFUSE_QUERY is required for semantic analysis (def-use sites)
extract_inheritance handler is required for class/interface analysis
No unsafe code without SAFETY comments
No unwrap/expect in production code (test exemptions via cfg_attr)
Queries must compile and match expected node kinds from grammar
test_coverage: Integration tests verify: (1) file parsing and element extraction (functions, classes, interfaces, enums); (2) inheritance extraction (extends/implements); (3) import statements; (4) def-use sites (writes, reads, assignments); (5) query compilation; (6) empty file handling. Language-specific tests in language module verify query correctness and handler logic.

library_findings.relevant_api: PHP grammar with function_definition, class_declaration, interface_declaration, enum_declaration, method_declaration node types; base_clause and class_interface_clause for inheritance
library_findings.notes: tree-sitter-php provides full PHP 8.x support including enums, attributes, match expressions, union types. Grammar uses base_clause (extends) and class_interface_clause (implements) as child nodes, not fields. method_declaration nodes appear inside class/interface/enum bodies.

library_findings.relevant_api: Query API with QueryCursor, capture_names(), Node.child_by_field_name(), Node.named_child(), Node.kind(), Node.parent()
library_findings.notes: Core parsing library; all language integrations depend on this version. Query syntax uses (node_type field: (child_type) @capture_name) patterns.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Minimal PHP Support (CSS-like pattern)
approaches.description: Add php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY capturing function_definition and class_declaration only; CALL_QUERY for function calls; no DEFUSE_QUERY, no inheritance extraction. Register in lang.rs EXTENSION_MAP with .php extension, add tree-sitter-php to Cargo.toml, wire in mod.rs get_language_info() and get_ts_language(), add integration tests.
pros: Follows CSS pattern which is minimal and working
Covers basic use case of function/class extraction

approaches.name: Approach 2: Full PHP Support (Java-like pattern)
approaches.description: Add php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY capturing function_definition, class_declaration, interface_declaration, enum_declaration, method_declaration; CALL_QUERY for function calls; REFERENCE_QUERY for type references; IMPORT_QUERY for use statements; DEFUSE_QUERY for local variables, assignments, identifier reads; extract_inheritance() handler walking base_clause and class_interface_clause child nodes to extract parent class and interface names. Register in lang.rs, Cargo.toml, mod.rs with full LanguageInfo struct. Add comprehensive integration tests covering all declaration kinds and inheritance scenarios.
pros: Complete PHP language support matching Java/Kotlin patterns
Enables def-use analysis for semantic queries
Supports all PHP declaration kinds (classes, interfaces, traits, enums)
Inheritance extraction enables call graph analysis
Consistent with project's existing language coverage

approaches.name: Approach 3: Phased PHP Support (Minimal + Handlers)
approaches.description: Phase 1: Add basic php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY (no DEFUSE_QUERY, no extract_inheritance). Phase 2: Add DEFUSE_QUERY and extract_inheritance() in follow-up PR. Register in mod.rs and lang.rs immediately. This allows landing basic support quickly while deferring advanced features.
pros: Faster initial merge (basic support in 1-2 days)
cons: Requires two PRs instead of one
May not meet issue requirements if full support is expected

recommendation: Approach 2 (Full PHP Support). The project's architecture and existing language integrations (Java, Kotlin, Swift) demonstrate that complete support is the standard. The issue title 'add PHP language support' implies full support, not partial. The DEFUSE_QUERY is essential for the project's semantic analysis capabilities (def-use sites are used in call graph and data flow analysis). The extract_inheritance handler is required for class hierarchy analysis. Implementing the full pattern now avoids technical debt and ensures PHP support is on par with other languages. The implementation is medium complexity (300-400 LOC) and follows proven patterns from Java and Swift.
language_info_struct_citation:
pub struct LanguageInfo {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub language: Language,
    pub element_query: &'static str,
    pub call_query: &'static str,
    pub reference_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub import_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_trait_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub defuse_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub extract_function_name: Option<ExtractFunctionNameHandler>,
    pub find_method_for_receiver: Option<FindMethodForReceiverHandler>,
    pub find_receiver_type: Option<FindReceiverTypeHandler>,
    pub extract_inheritance: Option<ExtractInheritanceHandler>,
}
element_query_draft:
r"
(function_definition
  name: (name) @function_name) @function
(class_declaration
  name: (name) @class_name) @class
(interface_declaration
  name: (name) @interface_name) @class
(trait_declaration
  name: (name) @trait_name) @class
(enum_declaration
  name: (name) @enum_name) @class
(method_declaration
  name: (name) @method_name) @function
"
defuse_query_draft:
r"
(assignment_expression left: (variable_name (name)) @write.assign)
(assignment_expression left: (list_destructuring (variable_name (name)) @write.list))
(variable_declaration declarator: (variable_declarator name: (variable_name (name)) @write.local))
(foreach_statement value: (variable_name (name)) @write.foreach)
(foreach_statement key: (variable_name (name)) @write.foreach)
(catch_clause (catch_clause_variable (variable_name (name)) @write.catch))
(variable_name (name)) @read.usage
"
inheritance_walk_citation: In the tree-sitter-php grammar, a class_declaration node has three fields: 'name' (required), 'attributes' (optional), and 'body' (required). Inheritance is not captured as fields but as child nodes: base_clause (for extends) and class_interface_clause (for implements) appear as optional children between the name and body. To extract inheritance: (1) walk the class_declaration node's children; (2) find base_clause nodes and extract the name nodes they contain (these are the parent class names); (3) find class_interface_clause nodes and extract the name nodes they contain (these are the interface names). The grammar rule is: class_declaration: seq(optional(attributes), repeat(modifiers), keyword('class'), field('name', name), optional(base_clause), optional(class_interface_clause), field('body', declaration_list)). Source: https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php/blob/master/common/define-grammar.js
